justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: Claim Submission & Routing Module serves external users (R-01), Adjuster Workspace Module supports adjusters (R-02), and Feature Flag / Routing Service enables incremental claim-type migration (R-03).
justifications.performance_efficiency: Response Caching & Transformation Component with Azure Cache for Redis and BFF Orchestrator Component insulate the UI from 5s mainframe latencies, enabling sub-2s response times alongside asynchronous processing via Outbox Processor.
justifications.compatibility: Coexistence is thoroughly managed by Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer, Mainframe Adapter Component, and Integration Gateway, respecting legacy protocols (AMQP/HTTPS) and batch constraints without requiring frequent mainframe alterations.
justifications.usability: Web App Portal clearly distinguishes user personas, providing Claim Submission & Routing Module for customers/brokers and Adjuster Workspace Module for claims adjusters via dedicated, responsive React SPA components.
justifications.reliability: Zero data loss and deduplication (R-04) are ensured by Outbox Processor, Idempotency & Deduplication Filter, and Dual-Write / Sync Coordinator, supplemented by Circuit Breaker Component for fault tolerance.
justifications.security: Meets R-07 via Authentication Wrapper using MSAL.js for Active Directory SSO over OIDC/OAuth2, combined with API Router Component token validation and mTLS on Mainframe Adapter Component.
justifications.maintainability: Meets R-06 through Routing Engine Component and Configuration Cache Component, allowing fast single-day switchbacks. Temporal History & Rollback Component and modular services minimize migration blast radius.
justifications.portability: Accurately targets the hybrid on-premises and Azure West Europe topology using Azure Container Apps. However, high coupling to specific Azure PaaS (App Configuration, Service Bus) slightly limits multi-cloud portability.

PERF-01.justification: The BFF response caching component with Azure Cache for Redis decouples client response times from legacy latency. However, cache misses on unmigrated claim fragments might still incur mainframe delays unless pre-cached or synced eagerly.
sensitivity_points: Cache hit ratio in Azure Cache for Redis
Aggressive data pre-synchronization before user access
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency and memory cache overhead versus sub-second UI responsiveness

PERF-02.justification: Submissions are captured in Azure SQL and buffered via the Outbox Processor and Azure Service Bus. This absorbs sudden traffic spikes entirely in Azure, shielding the mainframe and batch windows from load surges.
sensitivity_points: Service Bus queue storage capacity and dead-letter monitoring
Batch window scheduling policy in Integration & Sync Service
tradeoffs: Deferred batch delivery to mainframe versus immediate customer submission acceptance

AVAIL-01.justification: Transactional persistence in the Azure Claims Database combined with durable queuing in the Outbox Processor isolates the submission ingestion path from mainframe downtime during nightly batch windows.
sensitivity_points: Database availability during mainframe offline windows
tradeoffs: Eventual synchronization with mainframe versus continuous 24/7 online claim submission

AVAIL-02.justification: The architecture incorporates Durable Functions, transactional Outbox, and an Idempotency & Deduplication Filter backed by Azure SQL, ensuring reliable retries, exactly-once processing semantics, and automated state reconciliation.
sensitivity_points: Deduplication window duration and key uniqueness in Azure SQL
tradeoffs: Processing latency added by deduplication lookups versus strict transactional consistency

MOD-01.justification: The Feature Flag / Routing Service with Azure App Configuration enables instant, fine-grained routing adjustments per claim type. The Anti-Corruption Layer minimizes mainframe contract shifts, satisfying the one-day switch-back requirement.
sensitivity_points: Propagation latency of Azure App Configuration flag changes
Granularity of claim type routing rules
tradeoffs: Routing middleware evaluation overhead versus operational agility and zero-downtime rollbacks

MOD-02.justification: The Web App Portal and API Gateway are completely insulated from mainframe legacy dependencies. Retiring the mainframe only requires removing the Anti-Corruption Layer and sync components without UI refactoring.
sensitivity_points: Decoupling of BFF contracts from legacy data models
Completeness of the Azure Claims Database schema
tradeoffs: Maintaining dual schemas during transition versus seamless retirement without frontend rewrite

SEC-01.justification: While token validation and authentication via Active Directory are implemented at the gateway, fine-grained tenant isolation and claim-level authorization logic (e.g., verifying broker ownership of specific claims) are not explicitly detailed.
sensitivity_points: Fine-grained role and claim-based access control enforcement in BFF
Audit logging completeness for unauthorized resource access attempts
tradeoffs: Centralized gateway policy enforcement versus distributed domain-level authorization checks

SEC-02.justification: Single sign-on via Active Directory across modern and legacy tiers allows central identity revocation. However, active JWT lifetime and token revocation caching in API Management/BFF must be strictly configured under 15 minutes.
sensitivity_points: JWT access token expiration and refresh token lifetimes
Token revocation cache invalidation frequency in API gateway
tradeoffs: Frequent token re-validation overhead versus rapid 15-minute access revocation
